'''''Armeria pungens''''', common name '''spiny thrift''', is a rare plant of the genus ''[[Armeria]]'' of the family [[Plumbaginaceae]].

==Description==
''Armeria pungens'' grows in small shrubs, reaching heights of about {{convert|80|cm}}. The stems are lignified at the base, robust, highly branched. Leaves are glabrous, linear to lanceolate, pointed, about {{convert|60|-|150|mm}} long and about {{convert|1|-|3.5|mm}} wide. Flower heads are pale pink, gathered in globose inflorescences at the top of long [[pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]. Flowering period extends from May through July.

==Distribution==
This plant is endemic to [[Italy]] ([[Sardinia]]), [[France]] ([[Corsica]]), [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]].

==Habitat==
This small shrub grows in coastal sand-dunes and beaches, at an elevation of about {{convert|0|-|1|m}} above sea level.
